propositions: The query ticket's digest is re-sent in the user message on every call in a batch (12/12), consuming full-price tokens despite the system prompt being byte-identical.
Moving the invariant query digest from the user message into the system prompt would place it in the cacheable prefix block, enabling 1 write + N-1 cheap reads instead of N full-price reads.
The measured cache floor for the standard model class is 1024 tokens, not 4096, establishing that prefix caching is achievable on this request path.
The hoisted system prefix (846 tokens) falls short of the 1024 floor, resulting in +936 input tokens (+5.8% regression) with zero cache reads or writes.
Precision is preserved on all 12 ordered pairs (relations and shared_artifact unchanged), confirming the pointer-for-digest substitution does not degrade judge quality.
The relocation is necessary but insufficient to reach the cache floor; batching candidates per call is the complementary lever to close the 149–296 token gap.
